Episode 250. Ziffle and Kinzelo (1)
June 2, 1804, Tower of History.

Ziffle was almost finished with the task of merging the 'Holy Land' with the Tower of History. As a result, the area around the Tower had become so complex that even Valeria found it difficult to examine the records.
"How surprising. I had expected the Barmel Alliance to come first..."
At the top of the tower, Kelliark just met a person who had just descended from the sky.
"I didn't expect you to come before them."
Bligiet.
It was the avatar of the Sun God, in the form of Temar. He was wrapped in even more radiance than when he first met Ban, because he had consumed more flesh on his way here.
This meant he had become more rank and powerful. Yet, Kelliark seemed to think that he posed no threat to him at all.
[You knew I would come, yet you still tell such obvious lies, Kelliark Ziffle.]
A smile formed on Kelliark’s lips.
As Bligiet said, he had known about this situation beforehand. The Origin Stone had predicted Bligiet's arrival to the exact second.
Now it was time to see if the words Bligiet was about to utter would also match.
"If I have caused you displeasure, I apologize. Bligiet, avatar of the Sun God."
[You create terrible things to escape my insight, dare to predict me, and even occupy another of my avatars. It's no wonder I am displeased.]
The other avatar, referred to by Bligiet, was Ziffle's 'Holy Land'.
Currently, the Tower of History was in constant motion, and its location couldn't be accurately determined even with record magic.
But Bligiet found the tower in one try because he could sense the Holy Land. The Holy Land itself was an avatar of the Sun God, just like Bligiet.
Kelliark shrugged his shoulders and waved his hand toward the ground.
Then a table and chairs, along with a teapot and cups, formed on the empty floor. They appeared as if they had always been there.
A grotesque power mimicking 'the complete me'.

Bligiet realized just now that Kelliark's Origin Stone had already reached such a realm. Therefore, he also understood that he could not have the upper hand in negotiations with Kelliark. It was a series of humiliations for him since his resurrection.
Kelliark sat down first and gestured towards a chair for Bligiet.
"I'm still not adept at handling this power, so I'm not sure if the tea leaves will suit your taste."
The Origin Stone has already finished investigating you.
Bligiet, understanding this, sat down.
[I was captured by your device as soon as I was resurrected. I don't particularly like the scent.]
"It's a pity. Perhaps it reflects the taste of another avatar. It needs adjustment."
Uncomfortable.
Bligiet felt insulted by every word of Kelliark. To think that a mere imitator of a god was mocking him.
However, he couldn't attack Kelliark. Killing him was out of the question, and he might even be 'consumed' by the other avatar.
[Malugia... I'm curious how my other avatar, which you now call Elona Ziffle, ended up as your weapon.]
“There is quite an interesting story about that, would you like to hear it?”
[No. I know all about the pathetic history of your family that started with Reginald Ziffle. What I'm curious about is why Malugia allowed itself to be captured by you.]
"Captured?"
For the first time, the smile disappeared from Kelliark's lips.

[Malugia is the largest avatar of destruction. When we split into many, Malugia sought to destroy and erase everything. Not just the world we created, but even ourselves. Malugia was destruction incarnate.]
Therefore, Malugia was in conflict with almost all avatars, including Bligiet who wanted to rebuild the world. Malugia's goal was nothing but to return the world to nothingness.
This was new information for Kelliark. It also meant he hadn't been informed of this in advance by the Origin Stone.
"An interesting story."
[Malugia chose you to drive the world into complete destruction, that's the assumption that comes to mind immediately. Otherwise, there's no reason for Malugia to be captured by you.]
"Then it means my family and I have fallen into a trap. This is troubling."

[Perhaps. We do not change. The avatar that wants to maintain will continue to maintain, the one that wants to rebuild will rebuild, and the one that seeks destruction will seek destruction. From beginning to end, they never change.]
"If Malugia was such a powerful being, there would have been more opportunities to destroy the world in ancient times than now. Why choose us in such a complicated way?"

[You think a powerful being can do anything. To some extent, that's true, but the world we created isn't so simple. There are too many unnecessary variables. The sun cannot be opposed by anyone, but in truth, you can avoid it just by covering your eyes with your hand, can't you?]
Kelliark's eyes narrowed.
It was astonishing information. However, even if it were true, it wouldn't significantly impact the current situation for Ziffle.
After all, Elona was destined to be discarded after the final battle. Kelliark focused his attention not on the information but on discerning Bligiet's intentions.
The reason why he brought up this topic was clear.
"Honestly, I just thought it wouldn't be bad to meet the creator of the world... But just now, Lord Bligiet, you have proven yourself to be of some value."
It was a negotiation.
Bligiet sought out Ziffle to remove the 'Airan' constraint. And he brought up the story about Elona, or Malugia, as a bargaining chip to lead the deal successfully.
[I will protect you from Malugia.]
"Ha ha ha...!"
Kelliark leaned back and burst into laughter. After a good laugh, he met Bligiet's eyes again.
Of course, Kelliark had already found a way to perfectly dispose of Elona Ziffle. Even if the control through the Holy Crown went awry, he could handle Elona whenever the right time came.
But the more safety measures, the better. Especially if it's a predictable avatar of the Sun God.
"Ah, how disrespectful of me. From what I see, it seems unlikely that Lord Bligiet could do anything to Elona. But still..."
Whooosh-!

Suddenly, about a dozen green windows floated near Kelliark. They contained information about Bligiet, written in a language only he could understand. Bligiet was becoming accustomed to this human's irreverence.
"If the avatars that could be called allies of Lord Bligiet join together, it might not be impossible."
[I will awaken them.]
"But will those avatars really agree to this humiliating deal with Lord Bligiet? They might even join forces to attack us."
[You speak with false intent, Kelliark Ziffle. Even without insight, anyone can see the greed in your eyes, seeking to use us.]

"I and my family, as humans, want to rule the world, not become a sole deity like Lord Bligiet. So, shouldn't I make an effort not to lose my human senses? Otherwise, I might start thinking and acting like an immortal like Lord Bligiet."
Ziffle fundamentally differed from Kinzelo or the Sun God Cult. For Ziffle, the power of the Sun God was merely a means, not an end in itself.
"What Lord Bligiet wants in return is to remove the constraint on Temar's body, imposed by Airan Bement."
Bligiet nodded his head.
"In exchange for doing that, if Elona Ziffle gets out of control someday, Lord Bligiet will protect us. And one more thing..."
[After Airan's constraint is resolved, you want to possess the body of Temar.]
"Yes. It's just a cumbersome shell for Lord Bligiet, but it's a character with a deep story for us. Shall we proceed with this contract?"
[I agree to it.]
Then the green windows disappeared, and flames rose near Kelliark. It was the power of the Seal of Fire, the authority of Shinu born from the Sun God.
"This oath will be enforced by the power of Shinu, a god born from the Sun God. Compared to the freedom you will gain, Lord Bligiet, this is a minor humiliation. Please place your hand here."
Bligiet reached his hand towards the flames that appeared in front of Kelliark. The flame coiled around his arm like a snake. It signified that the contract was complete.
"As you know, this contract can be broken at any time before the process begins. If you find another solution before I remove Airan's constraint, simply disperse this flame."
Bligiet looked at the flame coiling around his left arm for a while.
[How much time will you need?]

"It's a task that involves changing the history of the oldest mortal in the world, so it will take at least half a year. It could be shorter if the enemies stay put, but that's unlikely. Look, a dimensional gate will open here 7 seconds after I finish speaking."
Exactly 7 seconds later, as Kelliark said, a steel dimensional gate opened. It was Orgal's dimensional gate.
However, those who emerged from the gate were not the usual protagonists of Kinzelo.
They were black figures with a human-like appearance. Kelliark frowned upon seeing them and sighed.
"Helluram. That monster, which could be called the descendant of Lord Bligiet, is targeting me. These creatures, they are called the Abyss Legion."
Note: Origin Stone/Source Stone/Demon Stone
